prerequisites: Familiarity with graphic user interfaces of modern operating systems
Proficiency in office applications and communication services

learning_outcomes.text: Basic knowledge on the use and programming of computers, operating systems, databases and computer programs with application in engineering.
Know and identify the main hardware and software components of a computer.
Know the syntax of a high-level programming language.
Know algorithms that solve classic problems (sorting, searching).
Use a high-level programming language integrated development environment (IDE).

Develop the capacity for abstraction and discipline as a basis for analyzing automatic information processing problems and decomposing them into manageable parts using modular design techniques and proposing a solution architecture.
Design algorithms that solve the different parts of a problem using detailed design techniques (structured programming).
Represent complex information models by appropriate selection and combination of data structures.
Build programs (implement algorithms that solve different problems in a high-level programming language).

syllabus_topics: Style guidelines for C language programming. Variables
Beyond vectors. Additional data types in C.
Functions as parameters. Pointers to functions
PR1 Fundamentals of working with GitHub
PR2-LAB Integrated programming environment / Programming with C in VS-Code
PR9-LAB Validation and closing of previous practices
PR17-LAB Validation and closing of previous practices
teaching_methods: Lectures/participative classes: Transmission of knowledge, fostering critical thinking
Theoretical-practical classes: Problem solving, program design examples
Laboratory tasks: Program construction (design, coding, and testing)
Tutorials: Resolution of doubts on theoretical/practical aspects, debugging errors in student-built programs
Autonomous study: Study of theoretical content and presented examples
Autonomous work: Program implementation (coding and testing)
assessment_rules: The course grade (100 points) is based on a final exam (85 points), laboratory practices (10 points), and student self-assessment (5 points). The grading formula is: Course Grade = Exam + Practices + Self-assessment. To pass, the total score must exceed 50 points, with a minimum of 5 points in Practices ('Apto') and a minimum of 35 points in the Exam. If minimums are not met, the final grade will be the minimum of the practice and exam scores. For the single final evaluation and extraordinary calls, all laboratory practices must be completed 100% and defended, and an exam (potentially including practical exercises in the laboratory) must be taken.
